summary: Revision 1 correctly returned HUMAN_REQUIRED: no fork-specific verified evidence existed in the repository and this session's environment could not reach primary-text hosts directly. The Director independently verified Cheiro's Palmistry for All (1916) against two independent public-domain transcriptions and recorded a controlling boundary in .ai-ops/evidence/PP-RELAY-047-cheiro-fate-line-branch.md. Revision 2 drafted the article within that narrow boundary. Added src/content/blog/beginner/forked-fate-line-meaning.md, item 18 from docs/editorial-backlog.md's Next 25 list (69 -> 70 published blog posts). The article first distinguishes a fork (the line itself dividing into two continuing strands) from a branch (an offshoot while the main line continues) and a break (a gap), then covers the single verified formation: a lower/origin fork with one strand toward the Mount of Venus and the other toward the Mount of Moon (Luna), which Cheiro associated with romance/passion strongly influencing career or life direction. It explicitly states that Palmistry Path does not have verified evidence for a terminal/top fork meaning (including the commonly repeated 'two careers' claim) or for any Jupiter/Apollo/Mercury/Saturn mount-directed fork synthesis, and declines to generalize the Venus/Moon reading to other fork locations. Direct observation, Cheiro's named historical interpretation, and Palmistry Path's own editorial stopping point are kept in a dedicated, clearly separated section. Added one sentence to fate-line.md's existing branches paragraph distinguishing fork from branch and linking to the new article; the sibling fate-line-branches-meaning.md (unverified terminal-fork prose) was not read as evidence, not modified, and not linked from the new article, per task scope.

Terminal/top forks and Jupiter/Apollo/Mercury/Saturn mount-directed fork synthesis are named explicitly as declined, unverified claims rather than silently omitted.
